partha_chatterjee.description: Partha Chatterjee studies colonial nationalism and the changing practices of imperial power. His work joins political theory and anthropology to historical research on colonial and postcolonial India. In his interview about The Black Hole of Empire, he explains how a local story of Calcutta and its memorial becomes the spine of a wider inquiry into concepts and practices of empire. He also identifies a lesson from Subaltern Studies: popular cultural forms can be analysed alongside elite political discourse. These are selective historical methods rather than a claim that one account exhausts empire.
